title: Gospel of Christ Jesus
paragraphs: Before we even start, I just want to thank you for deciding to sit with me. Every now and then, I will be hosting a session where we can sit together and talk. As Apostle Paul writes to the Colossians, in the same way, I may not be physically present with you or sitting with you, but I am there with you in spirit. So grab a cup of coffee or tea. I cannot promise that I will host these sessions regularly, but as the Holy Spirit inspires me, I will be sharing thoughts and ideas. When I say, “sit with me,” some of you might DM me and ask, “Why not make videos, Christina?” So here is my explanation: I am an introverted and shy person by nature, and yet I do not want to miss any opportunity to preach the Gospel of Christ to all creation. So here I am, taking advantage of technology. I am excited to start our first session. Sit back and read this with an open mind. As we reach the end, I hope your mind will be renewed, because transformation comes through the renewing of the mind. Having mentioned my passion for the Gospel, let us talk about the Gospel of Christ. As we read in Romans chapter 1, let us take a look.
[16] For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth; to the Jew first, and also to the Greek.

Paul says that he is not ashamed of the Gospel, and the word “gospel” simply means “good news.” What is this good news all about? It is the news of Christ! Paul continues by saying that this good news of Jesus Christ carries the power to offer salvation. Let us look at the same verse in The Passion Translation.

[16] I refuse to be ashamed of the wonderful message of God’s liberating power unleashed in us through Christ! For I am thrilled to preach that everyone who believes is saved—the Jew first, and then people everywhere!
From the verse above, we understand that this wonderful news of Jesus Christ reveals God's liberating power, which is found through Christ.

Let me amaze you. The Greek word often associated with “salvation” is *sōzō*. Its meaning is broader than forgiveness of sins alone. It can convey ideas such as healing, deliverance, and being made whole. Let me say this: you have no idea how powerful the Gospel is—the power of salvation! This Gospel inspires people who listen with open hearts to desire the life of Christ and to see His glory revealed in their physical lives. The Gospel of Christ invites those who receive this good news to experience life with Jesus as He transforms them daily to become more like Him. You are a temple of Christ, and you are one with Him. Let us talk about this more later, but for now, let us stay on the topic of the Gospel. Let us move to the next verse.
[17] For therein is the righteousness of God revealed from faith to faith: as it is written, The just shall live by faith.
Paul establishes that the righteousness of God is revealed in the Gospel. The true Gospel of Christ reveals the righteousness of Jesus Christ.
Did Paul mention anywhere that your righteousness or mine would be revealed? A big no! The good news of Jesus always reveals God's holiness and righteousness. And guess what?

According to 2 Corinthians 5:21, God made Jesus, who knew no sin, to be sin for us, so that through Him we might become the righteousness of God. You might say, “But Christina, I do not feel righteous.” Let us read verse 16 again.
[16] For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth.
Let us stop right there. It says, “to every one that believeth.”

Yes, it is a leap of faith—faith in JESUS and in the finished work of the CROSS. So wherever you are, just say, “Thank You, God, for making me righteous through Christ.” By believing this, you are demonstrating God-kind of faith, as it is written in verse 17: “The just shall live by faith.”

This is the good news: your actions or works of the flesh do not define your righteousness. It is God's goodness that qualifies you to receive every good thing and blessing. Salvation is described in Scripture through ideas such as righteousness, wholeness, prosperity, deliverance, and protection. This is called good news because, through faith and belief in Jesus Christ, you receive what you could never earn by your own efforts. When the Gospel of Jesus Christ is preached, it empowers people to receive salvation. In this way, not only is your eternity secure, but your life on this earth is also transformed. You are a new creation; the old has passed away. You begin to turn away from your past, grow thirstier for the Word and prayer, and become more like Christ—hating sin and embracing righteousness. When Jesus is preached, there is divine empowerment to overcome sin and death.

There may still be times when you fall. You will make mistakes, and you may fall into sin, but you can get up, dust yourself off, and walk with God again. No toddler walks perfectly on their first attempt. You need your Father to hold you up on this journey, and God your Father will always hold your hand; He will never let it go. This is the Gospel of Christ. Preach Jesus, and this is how a soul is saved. Let us go deeper later, when we talk about righteousness and the reality of righteousness. Thank you for taking the time to read this.
